items.note: The prompt treats this as an open choice of a vector database. It never says the real decision is whether to stay on pgvector or move to a dedicated vector DB. pgvector is just one of six candidates, and the question about Postgres doesn't fill the gap.
It asks for the vector count and dimensions in the interview, but never states 5M vectors at 1536 dimensions or growth of about 1M per quarter.
It asks whether the team already runs Postgres, but never states Postgres 16 on AWS RDS.
Budget is only asked about. The under-$500-per-month limit is never given.
It asks about filtering support in general, but never says queries must filter by tenant_id or that the system is multi-tenant.
The person wanted at most 4 options. The prompt requires 6 candidates (pgvector, Qdrant, Weaviate, Milvus, Pinecone, Chroma) and allows a 7th.
It asks for a comparison table and one primary recommendation. Adding a runner-up and risks doesn't undercut the single clear pick.
It says the space changes quickly and asks for current sources, but never sets a 12-month recency limit.
It never says to do a wide scan and then go deep on the top 2. Instead, every candidate gets the same depth.
